scope: Day-1A: the last road bend through arrival, Sext at the gate, reception, guest room, first solo route, the meal with William, a short free period and the first Nones transition. Design intent from story-council/day-1/OPUS_DAY1_DESIGN.md S1–S5, a reduced S8 and Nones; nothing after the first Nones.

status.verified: VERIFIED for automated checks and the instrumented walks listed here
status.experientially_validated: NOT RUN — no person other than the implementer's own capture review has played, listened or used the input

implemented: Day-1A is the default native mode (`--mode=day1a`); the Phase-1 proof stays intact behind `--mode=proof` and its scenarios.

World: seven new section exports from the browser builders (gate, guest house with the outside stair and upper cell, flower garden, church west front, western context, western gardens, Aedificium exterior) plus the six Phase-1 cells; a 232 × 176 m terrain patch at 1 m with a walkable mask, a 4 m coarse ring to r 215 m, a polar far ring to 9.5 km, 1 300 trees in 13 groups with the browser's atlas shader; all collision derived from the same export.

A deterministic scenario director (no scene dependencies) with stable actor identities, an authored way graph (139 nodes, 156 edges), walk limits, beats road → Sext at the gate → gate opens → reception → to the cell → second bundle (solo route) → meal → free period → Nones → after Nones → end.

William's lead/wait controller on the road: 5–8 m ahead at 1.72 m/s, eases to the boy's pace past 6.5 m, waits at authored look points when the gap passes 12 m and resumes at 5 m; an overtaking boy is followed (one gentle line, no reprimand). On the way to the cell the cellarer (and William with him) eases off and waits for a lagging guest.

Adso: first-person sleeves and hands, a shadow-casting body, carrying the bedding bundle, the chest, a bucket and wet hose, sitting on the stool and benches (getting up always available, onto clear floor), eating at the meal; no stats or inventory.

Cast: William, the porter, the cellarer, Tebaldo, Nuto, Fulco, Rainaldo and ten anonymous brothers; people are known by description until a name is heard (people memory); an internal observation log fed only by what was actually looked at.
The meal question “What have you seen so far?” offers the player's own observations (up to three plus “Nothing much yet”); nothing is scored.

Nones: the bell from the belfry, brothers close their books and walk to their stalls, Tebaldo/Fulco/the cellarer go too, Nuto pauses at the well, the cloister empties, the office begins once the brothers are in their stalls and is heard through the church's openings; no teleport, no freeze, no cutscene; stays playable if Adso ignores it.
Versioned Day-1A save (`abbey-day1a-save` v1, its own file) with autosaves at the cell, after the meal and at the end; a proof save offered to it is rejected and never overwritten.

Local-only telemetry (user://day1a/telemetry): William's lead on the road and to the cell, waits, overtakes, solo-route hesitation/wrong turns/time, free-period time and talks, people met, Nones attendance and time to notice the brothers moving.
Minimal UI: interaction prompt, subtitles with the speaker as known, numbered replies, pause menu with text size, captions and look sensitivity, an end card after the first Nones.

Benchmarks/validation scenarios: day1-walk (five walker styles), day1-cycles (ten real-time residency loops), day1-shots, day1-cast (with head close-ups), day1-graph-audit; run_benchmarks.sh day1_walk/day1_cycles.

deviations: The first full view of the Aedificium is staged inside the gate court: in this reconstruction the enclosure wall and the road's approach hide it from the last bend (recorded in shared/provenance/reconstruction-decisions.json).
Flower-garden hedges were given entrances where the alleys meet them (browser builder change, recorded as RECON).

The reconstructed postern is walled up natively and its track removed from the trodden-snow field; Aedificium interior sound emitters are not loaded; the Phase-1 skull altar, ossuary stair cell and the porch figure are absent in Day-1A mode but untouched in proof mode.
Clock compression: road to meal runs on authored beats; the free period passes 12.5 game minutes per real minute (×6 sitting on a bench), Nones 7 per real minute. No clock is shown.
known_issues: First run of a fresh package: two 0.54–0.59 s stalls in the free period (not repeated on the next run); likely first-use shader/pipeline compilation — a shader warm-up during loading would remove them.
Process memory crept ≈ 3 MiB per loop over loops 3–10 of the residency cycles (within the 10 % gate); a longer soak is needed before calling it flat.
Experience is unvalidated: no other person has played, listened or used a controller; whether William feels like a person and whether ordinary life is compelling are open questions, not results.
William is a stand-in (designed monk_c body, Franciscan tint, satchel), not a bespoke model; Tebaldo has 11 lines (under the 20–30 allowance) and his fussiness rests mostly on routing and timing.

The recorded walks are slow (≈0.5 m/s at 1×); playback is quickened up to 2.35×, so William at 1.72 m/s slides his feet somewhat, and the formal walk's passing phase shows a deep knee bend in side view (the browser's clip).
Nuto's limp is a timing warp plus a small hip drop on the ordinary walk: legible as uneven, subtle at distance; needs a human eye.
Nones: the office begins about 65 s after the first stroke (brothers walk from the far walks at 1.05 m/s); may feel long.

The chant at the guests' place measures −36 to −53 dBFS RMS (0.5 s windows, mean −42.5) against −31.4 for the bell and the walk in and −36.4 on the garth before the bell; plausible for 8 m from the choir but unconfirmed by ear.

Two early Nones recordings had exact digital silence on the master bus; after guarding all Day-1A sound positions and the chant level/cut-off it no longer occurs (whole-day probe and final recording clean), but the original trigger was not conclusively identified.

Scripted walkers still stall briefly (3 s each, then re-plan) beside the cell table and at a cloister pier; a person can step round, and the graph's capsule-sweep audit passes, but the cell is cramped.
Small things on the tray sit close together; the prompt follows the crosshair, and “Get up” shows only when nothing else is aimed at (any movement key also stands Adso up).
People have a soft personal space, not hard colliders: a person walking into Adso nudges him aside rather than stopping.
Lines are original game fiction pending canon and forward-spoiler review by a finished-book reader; the reception staging deviates (the Aedificium is first seen fully inside the gate court).
Day-1A keeps every cell resident, so the Phase-1 stair-head unload hitch does not occur in Day-1A; it is not fixed in the proof.
Windows runtime, W1/W2, controller and human listening: NOT RUN.
Evidence JSON contains absolute local paths (user data and build locations), as the Phase-1 evidence does.
playable_path: Road (last bend, mule on a lead, William a few metres ahead; look points: the valley, a pine trunk, the wall, the tower) → the gate during Sext: closed; the porter opens as the bell finishes (about 22 s in)
Gate court: the porter steadies the mule (hold the halter), the first full view of the Aedificium, the cellarer comes from the church, names are heard
Take the bedding and follow the cellarer and William down the avenue, round the church front, across the flower garden, up the outside stair to the third guest cell; put the bedding on the straw
Second bundle, first solo route: back down to the gate for the chest and up again to the cell (William waits in the cell; no arrows)

Meal in the cell: Tebaldo brings the tray and fusses, sit at the table, eat, wring out William's hose; William asks “What have you seen so far?”; Nuto comes for the tray; William leaves for the Abbot (offstage)
Free period (about 5–8 minutes): Fulco on the cloister walk, Nuto at the well (carry a bucket), Rainaldo at a lectern, Tebaldo passing, benches to sit on
Nones: the bell, the cloister empties into the church, the office; then a brief free beat and the end card

audio.fixed_during_validation: Two earlier Nones recordings contained stretches of exact digital silence on the master bus. 1_william_walk_carries_character.why: He leads by route progress 6.5–8 m ahead, turns his head to authored sights, waits only when the boy falls ~12 m behind (once, at the pine trunk, for the slow walker) and follows an overtaking boy with one easy line; with the cellarer he eases off for a lagging guest. But the body is a stand-in and the recorded walk is quickened to his pace with some foot slide; no person has yet judged whether he reads as a person.

2_abbey_inhabited_before_investigation.why: The porter and two mules, a cellarer who escorts, Tebaldo fussing with the tray, Nuto at the well (with a bucket to carry), Fulco reading, Rainaldo at a lectern, ten brothers reading in the walks and six leaving the church after Sext, a far hammer, crows. It is a small cast with simple routines; the avenue and gardens are empty for long stretches and nobody has played it.

3_guest_house_route_learnable_without_ui.why: Every walker style repeated the route without hints (68–87 s out, the confused walker took a wrong turn at the church front and recovered) along strong landmarks (avenue, church front, hedged garden, outside stair). Those are scripted walkers with a map; no unfamiliar person has tried it.

4_nones_changes_the_abbey.why: Bell from the belfry, books closed, the walks empty into the stalls, the office begins only when the brothers are in place and is heard through the openings; nothing freezes and staying out works. The 65 s wait before singing, uniform walking and a quiet chant level are unjudged by ear or eye.

5_characters_good_enough_for_narrative.why: Designed bodies with habits, faces, tonsures and props hold up at walking and speaking distance and are distinguishable (Nuto's cap and beard, Fazio's leather cap, Tebaldo's keys, Fulco's youth). Close-ups show jagged tonsure edges, primitive caps, a deep-knee formal walk and William as a stand-in.
